newsitem.title: USA: Fire aboard Cunard cruise ship kills crewman.
newsitem.headline: Fire aboard Cunard cruise ship kills crewman.

text.p: Fire broke out in a linen locker aboard a cruise ship near the Bahamas on Sunday, killing a crew member and forcing hundreds of passengers to prepare to abandon ship, the U.S. Coast Guard said.

The Cunard cruise ship Vistafjord, carrying 991 passengers and crew on a trans-Atlantic voyage, radioed for help just a few hours after leaving Fort Lauderdale, Florida, bound for Funchal on the Portuguese island of Madeira, the Coast Guard said.

Hundreds of passengers were mustered on deck at emergency stations and other ships in the area were diverted to the scene in case evacuation was needed, but the fire did not spread beyond the ship's laundry, officials said.

"Any fire at sea looks serious. We were making the preparations as soon as we got the call," U.S. Coast Guard Petty Officer David French said. "We asked the crew to brief the passengers, asking them to prepare to abandon ship."

New York-based Cunard Line Ltd., owner of the 627-foot (190-metre) Bahamian-registered vessel, said a German crewman in his twenties died as a result of the fire. The exact cause of death had not been determined, spokesman Bill Spears said.
Another crew member suffered a broken ankle and a passenger broke an arm, the company said.
The fire was extinguished after the ship pulled into port at Freeport, Bahamas, more than three hours after the crew radioed for help, a Coast Guard spokesman said.
The vessel put out a distress call while it was about 20 miles (32 km) south of Freeport, the Coast Guard said.

As its crew fought the fire and turned the ship toward Freeport, the Coast Guard dispatched a boat and a plane, and three other cruise ships, the Veendam, Destiny and Leeward, diverted in case passengers had to abandon ship, French said.
The Vistafjord arrived at Freeport near dawn and the crew, with help from Bahamian firefighters, extinguished the blaze within an hour, French said.
Cunard said smoke spread to cabins and passageways, but fire damage was contained to the linen locker area on the ship's third deck toward the stern.

Spears said the Vistafjord would remain in Freeport for at least two days and then was "more likely than not" to continue the cruise on an altered schedule. Passengers would be able to stay on board, he said.
"The majority are staying on board and may continue with the cruise," Spears said. "Some people may change their mind. One or two passengers have asked to return home."
The Coast Guard dispatched investigators to Freeport to investigate the cause of the fire.
"We know where it started ... but our investigators will have to go over to figure out why it started," French said.
